title: Use of Complementary and Alternative Treatments in Adolescent Obesity: A Narrative Review
content: Abstract: Adolescent obesity is a growing global health problem all around the world. We reviewed the use of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) treatment for adolescent obesity. We performed a PubMed and Scopus search of all articles on CAM treatments in adolescents aged 12–17 years and included all studies that had all or part of those ages. Out of 226 PubMed articles and 14 Scopus articles, 28 articles from PubMed and one article from Scopus fit our criteria. Most CAM studies that showed some improvement in BMI were acupuncture- and yoga-based. Herb- and supplement-based studies involving fish oil, purslane seeds, jujuba fruits, Korean-based Tae-umjowi-tang herbal formula, and Chinese capsules have shown promise. Studies based on mind-body interventions such as self-hypnosis, slow deep breathing, emotional freedom techniques, and Mandolean training have also shown a significant impact on adolescent obesity. Music skip rope, dance-based exergaming, kung fu, creative drama, aerobic exercise, and respiratory muscle endurance training are physical therapy-based interventions helpful in the management of adolescent obesity. Although many studies were RCTs, the individual studies were small in size. There may be a role in doing larger studies to generate more effective conclusions in future.
